classification.difficultyReason: Read "takes away four lots of this number from itself" as one lot minus four lots equals -3 lots, then divide to recover the number, an unscaffolded wording-to-model step.

content.prompt:
Ed thinks of a number. He takes away four lots of this number from itself. He is left with $-36$.

What was Ed’s original number?

answer.worked:
One lot minus four lots leaves $-3$ lots of the number.

$$-36\div(-3)=12$$

Check:

$$\begin{align*}12-4\times12&=12-48\\&=-36\end{align*}$$

Ed’s original number was $12$.
